title: Cost Habitat: adaptive workload profiler and safe-apply batch tuner
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an adaptive profiling and recommendation engine ("Cost Habitat") that synthesizes live workload fingerprints, KV/prefix cache hit patterns, and latency/cost tradeoffs to propose continuous batching parameter sets. Provide a safe-apply execution path (shadow simulation, canary apply, automated rollback triggers) so platform teams can deploy suggested configs without risking SLA regressions or cost-outliers.
comments: 2025-02-10 — Initial ticket created. Goal: replace ad-hoc batch knobs with model-driven profiles and an automated, safety-first apply pipeline.

2025-02-14 — Spike completed: collected week-long request traces from prod-metrics (sampled) and ran offline micro-simulations. Found three dominant workload archetypes: short-chat (<128 tokens, high arrival rate), long-completion (>1024 tokens, low QPS), and mixed multi-turn (low burst frequency but high KV reuse).

2025-02-20 — Architecture sync with infra: profiling agent will expose per-route fingerprints (seq_len_histogram, kv_hit_ratio, arrival_iec, burst_index). Agents will stream compressed fingerprints to a central selector service every 5m.

2025-02-28 — Prototype recommender implemented (heuristic rules + gradient-free search). Initial suggestions reduce per-token cost by ~12% on offline sims for short-chat cohort but introduced 8% p95 latency uplift in a few tail cases — identified root cause: over-aggressive coalescing when burst_index spikes.

2025-03-03 — Implemented safe-apply pipeline: (1) shadow-apply simulation for 1h using replayed requests, (2) canary rollout to 5% traffic with tighter SLO monitoring, (3) automated rollback if latency or error-rate exceeds configured thresholds. Added kill-switch to disable auto-apply.

2025-03-05 — Running cross-team review with SRE and PM. SRE requested a stricter rollback policy for high-sensitivity customers and a mechanism to pin route-level conservative profiles. PM asked for UX hooks in Console to accept/reject suggestions.
decision_log: 2025-02-21 — Chosen profiling cadence: 5m aggregated fingerprints (tradeoff: faster detection vs ingest cost).
2025-02-25 — Recommender strategy: hybrid approach (ruleset for safety + local search for fine-tune). Decided against pure ML blackbox model due to explainability/rollback needs.
2025-03-01 — Safe-apply stages finalized: shadow-sim -> canary -> ramp -> automated rollback. Canary default: 5% traffic for 30m with p95/latency and error-rate windows.
2025-03-04 — Threshold defaults: p95 latency increase <= +10ms OR +5% relative (whichever stricter), error-rate delta <= +0.1% absolute. Cost savings target >= 5% for apply to be considered.
2025-03-05 — Security review flagged KMS use for persisted profile storage; action created to add encryption-at-rest and audit logs in next sprint.
acceptance_criteria: Central profiler agent emits route fingerprints every 5m and is validated on two production clusters (canary and primary).
Recommender produces human-readable rationale for each suggested profile (e.g., "increase microbatch to 8 to improve GPU fill for short-chat; expected cost -12%; risk: p95 +6ms").
Shadow-apply simulation can replay 1h of sampled traffic and produce estimated latency/cost delta report within 15 minutes.
Canary rollout mechanism integrated with Console: operator can accept suggestion, schedule rollout, or reject. Canary runs at 5% for 30m by default.
Automated rollback triggers when monitored windows exceed configured thresholds, and rollback completes within 90s on average, verified in test harness.
Playbook documented in Confluence with rollback runbook, SLOs to monitor, and escalation path to SRE and product owners.
Unit/integration tests for recommender scoring rules and safe-apply orchestration included in CI; two end-to-end nightlies against staging cluster passing for 7 consecutive runs.
status_history: 2025-03-05 In Progress (safety review and canary validation)
